categories.main_business_segments: Con Edison operates through four primary business segments: (1) Consolidated Edison Company of New York (CECONY), which provides regulated electric, gas, and steam delivery services in New York City and Westchester County; (2) Orange and Rockland Utilities (O&R), which provides regulated electric and gas delivery services in southeastern New York and northern New Jersey; (3) Con Edison Clean Energy Businesses, which develops, owns and operates renewable energy infrastructure projects and provides energy-related products and services (classified as held for sale as of December 31, 2022); and (4) Con Edison Transmission, which invests in electric transmission projects and manages electric and gas assets through joint ventures.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The Utilities operate electric distribution and transmission systems, gas distribution networks, and steam generation and distribution infrastructure. CECONY operates steam-electric generating stations and steam-only generating stations for cogeneration. The Clean Energy Businesses develop and operate utility-scale renewable energy projects, primarily solar and wind generation facilities. Con Edison Transmission invests in electric transmission infrastructure and manages gas storage facilities. The companies employ advanced metering infrastructure (AMI), distributed energy resource management systems, and energy efficiency technologies.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The Utilities serve approximately 3.6 million electric customers, 1.1 million gas customers, and 1,530 steam customers in New York City, Westchester County, and parts of northern New Jersey. O&R serves approximately 0.3 million electric customers and 0.1 million gas customers. The Clean Energy Businesses sell renewable energy output under long-term power purchase agreements with utilities and municipalities across the United States. Con Edison Transmission serves transmission customers in New York and other northeastern states.
categories.geographic_coverage: Con Edison's primary operating regions are New York City, Westchester County, and parts of northern New Jersey. CECONY serves a 660-square-mile service area in New York City and Westchester County with a population exceeding nine million. O&R operates in a 1,300-square-mile service area in southeastern New York and northern New Jersey. The Clean Energy Businesses operate renewable energy projects across multiple U.S. states including California, Nevada, Arizona, Texas, New England, and the Mid-Atlantic region. Con Edison Transmission focuses on New York, New England, Mid-Atlantic, and Midwest transmission projects.
categories.supply_chain_position: Con Edison operates primarily in the midstream and downstream segments of the energy supply chain. The Utilities purchase electricity and natural gas from wholesale markets and suppliers, then deliver these commodities to end-use customers through their distribution networks. CECONY also generates electricity and steam for its customers. The Clean Energy Businesses operate in the upstream renewable generation segment, producing electricity from solar and wind projects. Con Edison Transmission invests in transmission infrastructure that connects generation sources to distribution networks.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Con Edison's strategic priorities include leading the clean energy transition, building the grid of the future, empowering customers to meet climate goals, and reimagining the gas system. The company is investing in advanced metering infrastructure, distributed energy resource management, energy storage, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and thermal energy networks. R&D initiatives focus on climate resilience, renewable energy integration, energy efficiency programs, and demand reduction technologies to support New York State's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act goals.
categories.revenue_model: Con Edison generates revenue primarily through regulated utility rate structures approved by state regulators. CECONY and O&R recover costs for electricity and gas delivery service through tariffs that include base rates, energy cost recovery mechanisms, and various surcharges and adjustment mechanisms. The Utilities also recover costs for energy efficiency programs, renewable energy credits, and other regulatory programs. The Clean Energy Businesses generate revenue from long-term power purchase agreements for renewable energy output and from energy-related products and services. Con Edison Transmission earns returns on its transmission investments through FERC-approved rate structures.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In New York State, Con Edison competes with four other major investor-owned utilities: National Grid plc, Avangrid Inc., National Fuel Gas Company, and CH Energy Group Inc., as well as state authorities NYPA and LIPA. The Utilities face competition from distributed energy resources, including solar generation, battery storage, and demand reduction programs. The Clean Energy Businesses compete in the renewable energy development market. Con Edison's regulated utility operations have limited direct competition due to geographic service territories, but face indirect competition from alternative energy sources and efficiency measures that reduce customer demand.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Con Edison reported 2022 net income of $1,660 million ($4.68 per share) compared to $1,346 million ($3.86 per share) in 2021. Adjusted earnings were $1,620 million ($4.57 per share) in 2022 versus $1,528 million ($4.39 per share) in 2021. The company's market capitalization was approximately $33.7 billion as of June 30, 2022. Capital investments totaled $4,465 million in 2022, with estimated investments of $4,809 million, $4,846 million, and $4,963 million for 2023-2025 respectively. The company maintains a common equity ratio of approximately 50.9 percent and investment-grade credit ratings.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Con Edison differentiates itself through its commitment to reliable, resilient, and safe energy delivery in densely populated urban areas, combined with leadership in the clean energy transition. The company emphasizes operational excellence, customer service, and community engagement. The Utilities offer revenue decoupling mechanisms that protect earnings from fluctuations in customer demand, energy efficiency and demand reduction programs, electric vehicle charging infrastructure, and renewable energy integration. Con Edison Transmission provides contracted returns on transmission investments supporting clean energy goals, while the Clean Energy Businesses offer long-term contracted renewable energy generation with stable cash flows.
